families.name: Classic greedy baselines
families.description: Textbook online rules as the priority: best fit (tightest residual), first fit (lowest index), worst fit (emptiest bin). Attempts 1, 2, 3.
families.boundary: Plain reference rules with no changes; tie-break or exact-fit tweaks of best fit go in F03, reorderings of its score go in F02.

families.name: Monotone transforms of best fit
families.description: Any strictly monotone reshaping of the residual score: squared, exponential, log, scaled, bonus or fullness terms. The argmax stays best fit, so packings are unchanged. Attempts 4-10.
families.boundary: Keeps best fit's ordering exactly; non-monotone residual scoring is F04, tie-break changes are F03.

families.name: Best-fit tie-break tweaks
families.description: Best fit with small changes to how near-ties or exact fits are resolved: oldest bin within 1 unit, exact-fit first, rounded residuals, small index penalty. Attempts 32, 56, 71, 82.
families.boundary: Changes only ties or near-ties of best fit; F02 leaves the ordering fully intact, and F04 reorders non-monotonically.

families.name: Fixed non-monotone residual table
families.description: A hand-set or offline-tuned step table (or spline) over the post-placement residual that ranks mid gaps below large ones. Break points are grid-swept, rescaled or annealed. Attempts 11-14, 61, 76.
families.boundary: One static table for all items; tables keyed by item size are F05, tables learned during the stream are F06.

families.name: Item-size-conditioned step tables
families.description: Several residual step tables, each picked by the arriving item's size class (C/3 threshold or quantile classes), tuned by hand or jointly by CMA-ES. Attempts 15, 79.
families.boundary: Choice between step tables by item size; switching between different heuristic types is F12.

families.name: Online adaptive step table
families.description: The residual table is learned during the stream from how often gaps of each size were later closed to zero. Attempts 73, 74, 75.
families.boundary: Table values come from observed gap-closure outcomes; F09 scores gaps from the item-size distribution instead.

families.name: Polynomial with index differencing
families.description: The FunSearch Weibull polynomial in capacity and item size, sign-flipped by bin size and differenced against a neighbouring bin, plus exponent, lag, sign, normalisation, sort-order and clipping variants. Attempts 16-21, 62, 63, 83.
families.boundary: Single polynomial-differencing score; adding a fill-probability term is F24, and blends with other heuristics are F15 or F16.

families.name: Harmonic size-class segregation
families.description: Items are split into size classes that pack into reserved bins or bin types: Harmonic-k, Refined Harmonic, cross-class leakage, or a new bin for every large item. Attempts 22-25, 70.
families.boundary: Hard bin segregation by item class; soft reservation of residual ranges inside shared bins is F18.

families.name: Empirical fill-probability lookahead
families.description: Best-fit score plus a term for the chance that a future item, estimated from past sizes (histogram, KDE, fitted Weibull, window, two-item convolution), fills the gap. Also covers expected-waste scoring. Attempts 26-31, 64, 65, 72, 77.
families.boundary: Scores a gap by the chance that it gets filled; F10 penalises gaps that can't be filled, and F21 matches exact seen sizes.

families.name: Fragment-avoidance penalty
families.description: Penalise placements that leave a gap smaller than the smallest seen item size (or a percentile or decaying estimate), optionally stacked on a step table. Attempts 33-36, 69.
families.boundary: A hard penalty below a size threshold; the graded probabilities of F09 fall outside it.

families.name: Randomised bin selection
families.description: Stochastic choice among feasible bins: a Gumbel-softmax over residuals, or epsilon-greedy mixing of first fit into best fit. Attempts 37, 38.
families.boundary: Randomness in the choice itself; deterministic rules sit in the other families.

families.name: Static rule switching by item
families.description: Picks a heuristic, or a stage of a staged rule, from the current item or its fit: polynomial for small items and table for large ones, or near-exact best fit first with polynomial fallback. Attempts 39, 81.
families.boundary: The switch depends on the current item or placement; F13 switches on stream feedback and F14 on dataset identity.

families.name: Feedback-driven heuristic selection
families.description: Picks a heuristic from online performance: switch to best fit when bin count runs over the L1 bound, or choose the best rule on the first 10% prefix. Attempts 78, 84.
families.boundary: Selection driven by measured performance during the stream; F12 switches on item features.

families.name: Dataset-identity switching
families.description: Picks the heuristic by bin capacity, which identifies the dataset. Violates G-ONLINE. Attempt 40.
families.boundary: Branches on the dataset itself; the legitimate online switches in F12 and F13 do not.

families.name: Ensembles of hand heuristics
families.description: Combines standardised step-table and polynomial scores by a linear blend, a rank sum or a per-bin max. Attempts 41, 42, 68.
families.boundary: Fixed blending of two existing heuristics' scores; blends learned over many features are F16.

families.name: Tuned linear feature score
families.description: A linear bin score over residual, item, fill-probability and polynomial features, with coefficients tuned by CMA-ES or random search under various objectives, seeds, populations and interleavings. Attempts 43-46, 48, 66, 67, 87.
families.boundary: Linear parametric score fitted offline; nonlinear learned models are F17.

families.name: Learned neural priority
families.description: A small MLP over bin features gives the priority, trained with evolution strategies. Attempt 47.
families.boundary: A nonlinear learned model, as opposed to F16's linear coefficients.

families.name: Bin reservation rules
families.description: Keeps certain bins for certain items: large gaps held back from small items, a cap on active bins, median-range gaps reserved for large items. Attempts 49, 50, 51.
families.boundary: Soft exclusion rules inside shared bins; F08 segregates bins permanently by item class.

families.name: Evaluator tooling and reproduction
families.description: Scorer infrastructure and measurements: incremental masks, L1 bound checks, validity checks, per-instance spread, reproducing the published FunSearch heuristics. Attempts 52-55, 88.
families.boundary: No new priority mechanism, only measurement or tooling, unlike every other family.

families.name: Semi-online lookahead buffer
families.description: Buffers arriving items and reorders them before placing (windowed FFD). Violates G-ONLINE. Attempt 57.
families.boundary: Reorders or looks ahead at real items; F09 only models the distribution.

families.name: Residual matches seen sizes
families.description: Prefers gaps equal to a previously seen unpaired item size, or close to multiples of the median seen size. Attempts 58, 59, 60.
families.boundary: Targets gaps equal to specific seen sizes; F09 uses probabilities over a range.

families.name: Residual clustering across bins
families.description: Prefers the bin whose new residual equals the most common residual among open bins, so gaps cluster. Attempt 85.
families.boundary: Shapes gaps around the open-bin population, not around item sizes as F21 does.

families.name: Hypothetical duplicate placement
families.description: Scores a bin by the residual left after placing a hypothetical second copy of the current item. Attempt 80.
families.boundary: Simulates a repeat of the current item; F09 uses the distribution of past sizes.

families.name: Polynomial plus fill probability
families.description: The index-differenced polynomial priority plus a weighted fill-probability term. Attempt 86.
families.boundary: Adds lookahead to F07's polynomial specifically; F16 learns a general feature blend.

families.name: other / unclassified
families.description: Attempts that fit no family.
